supportingDeclarations.applicability: At a nonzero producer output y the composed derivative kills v exactly when Jv is in the radial line through y.
At a unit state and orthogonal perturbation there is a linear consumer realizing any specified real tangent multiplier.
With a nonzero initial state, the initial normalization derivative kills radial multiples before the subsequent linear and normalization maps act.
At nonzero y with Jv orthogonal to y, post-normalization sends Jv to its inverse-radius-scaled value.
For unit input u and a nonzero tangent witness at nonzero y, there exists a linear producer sending u to that witness so it survives post-normalization.
A differentiable producer with nonzero output admits the chain rule for exact post-normalization.
For a differentiable producer with nonzero output, the actual derivative kills v exactly when the producer derivative sends v into the output radial line.
For a nonzero state and a consumer differentiable at its normalized direction, the derivative of the composed map kills every radial multiple.
For unit input u and a nonzero orthogonal witness at nonzero y, an affine producer with output y at u realizes survival of the radial derivative.
In a complete real inner-product space, at nonzero x with a loss differentiable at N(x), the composed gradient is the inverse-radius-scaled tangent projection of the loss gradient.
For a differentiable loss at N(x) with x nonzero, the squared norm of the unnormalized step is ‖x‖² plus the squared learning rate times the squared norm of the composed gradient.

formalScope.map: Exact normalization composed before or after a derivative map, plus a scalar loss composed with normalization.
formalScope.domain: real inner-product spaces for normalization; the downstream linear codomain may be a normed real space; the gradient result assumes a complete inner-product space
premises: Each normalization derivative used for a kernel or tangent claim is evaluated at its corresponding nonzero input.
The post-normalization kernel depends on where the producer Jacobian sends the input direction. Tangent gain requires an image orthogonal to the normalization input.
The gradient result assumes the stated gradient at the normalized point.
formalScope.extent: Local composition and gradient identities, and a checked two-dimensional affine-producer counterexample.
formalScope.claim: The post-normalization kernel is the producer-Jacobian preimage of the output radial line. The two-dimensional witness shows that an input radial direction can survive composition.
formalScope.studyBoundary: A product of Jacobians across recurrent steps needs an independently justified model of the composed maps and their varying radial and tangent directions.
